question: The spec's central measurement -- 'each ceremony step costs 2.3x what it did' -- does not survive re-derivation. Re-running the identical attribution over 255 sessions gives ratios from 1.01x to 2.96x depending on method choices that are all defensible; under the spec's OWN named breakdown (the four canonical step keys) the ratio is 1.01x and it is work, not ceremony, that rises; the flat-work control does not hold (+29% to +79%); and the 2026-08-07 cohort split is exactly the date Set 111 installed the instruments the post-cap cohort is measured with. The spec directs that 'any number that fails to reproduce is reported as a correction, and the corrected value is what the rest of the set uses' -- but there is no single corrected value here, because the quantity is method-dependent. Report a corrected ratio, report the range and decline to pick, or treat the reproduction as close enough and proceed on 2.3x?
decision: Report the range and decline to pick a corrected ratio; replace the 2.3x as the set's operative number with two taxonomy-independent measurements that do reproduce -- the marginal cost of a verification round (+17.9 min of loop span, R2 0.625) and recorded suite runtime (18.6 min/session). The session's Ends-with is satisfied by attributing the growth to NAMED, DATED causes, and the honest attribution is that the largest single cause of the apparent per-step rise is the arrival of the instruments on 2026-08-07, not a change in what ceremony costs. Sessions 2 and 3 inherit the corrected phase figures (loop 35.8 min, tail 12.6 min, latency 24% of the loop) and the two candidate numbers, not the 2.3x.

options.option: Report the range, decline a single corrected ratio, re-base the set on round cost and suite runtime (chosen)
options.consequence: The set keeps a measured foundation for Session 3's cuts without inventing a precision the data does not support. Costs the set its headline number and forces Session 3 to work from two figures rather than one. Nothing is deleted or cut on this basis, so the call is fully reversible by a later set that closes the stepKey vocabulary and re-measures.

options.option: Publish a single corrected ratio (e.g. the 1.71x burst-collapsed variant) as the new operative number
options.consequence: Preserves the spec's shape and gives Session 3 one number to work from, but launders a method choice into a fact. The same corpus yields 1.01x under the spec's own four-key breakdown, and any cut sized against 1.71x would be sized against an artifact of the classifier the orchestrator picked.

options.option: Treat +0.966 vs +0.947 min/day as a clean reproduction and proceed on 2.3x
options.consequence: Cheapest path and the duration trend genuinely does reproduce, but it carries the unsupported half forward into a session whose job is to DELETE things. This repo has been wrong about its own numbers three times in a week and every time it was the re-measuring session that caught it; this is that session declining to catch it.

reasoning: Judgment-shaped and therefore the orchestrator's under the rubric: it is a spec-vs-reality conflict, the first tiebreak (goal-over-letter) decides it, and no human-required class is touched. The spec's GOAL is that cuts trace to measured numbers; its LETTER asks for a single corrected value. Where the quantity is method-dependent, honouring the letter would defeat the goal by handing Session 3 a number precise enough to justify a deletion and not robust enough to survive one. Explicitly NOT a verification reduction: nothing here makes any loop stop earlier, and both surviving candidates that would reduce verification (C1's stop-earlier variant, C2 entirely) are recorded as operator-owned and are surfaced with their measurements rather than proposed. The decision is reversible -- it changes which numbers the set quotes, deletes nothing, and a later set that closes the stepKey vocabulary can re-derive a defensible ratio.

question: CORRECTION to this session's first journaled record. That record's closing sentence said Sessions 2 and 3 inherit 'the corrected phase figures (loop 35.8 min, tail 12.6 min, latency 24% of the loop)'. Verification round 1 raised a blocking Major establishing that the latency figure derives from ai_router/router-metrics.jsonl, which is gitignored (.gitignore:7) and untracked, against a spec requiring analysis over committed artifacts only. The journal is append-only and written by a sanctioned writer, so the original record cannot be edited. Restate the inheritance, or leave the stale parenthetical standing on the grounds that the deliverable document is now correct?
decision: Restate it here, in an appended record. Sessions 2 and 3 inherit ONLY committed-source values: verification loop 35.8 min, Step 8 tail 12.6 min (8.1 of it recorded suite runtime), marginal cost of a verification round 17.9 min of loop span, recorded suite runtime 18.6 min/session. NO LATENCY FIGURE IS INHERITED. The framework currently has no committed instrument for routed-call latency, so any claim about the model-latency share of the verification loop is unverifiable from a fresh checkout and may not be used to size a cut. The prior record's substantive decision -- report the 1.01x-2.96x range rather than a single corrected ratio, and re-base the set on round cost and suite runtime -- stands unchanged; only its parenthetical list of inherited figures is corrected.

options.option: Append a correcting record restating the inherited values (chosen)
options.consequence: The journal reads correctly end-to-end without anyone editing an append-only ledger, and a Session 2 or 3 orchestrator reading decisions.jsonl in order gets the corrected inheritance list. Costs one extra record.

options.option: Leave the stale parenthetical; the deliverable document is authoritative and is now correct
options.consequence: Cheaper, and defensible since s1-ceremony-attribution.md is the domain owner. But it leaves the exact defect the verifier found -- a non-reproducible number sitting in a list labelled as what the rest of the set inherits -- alive in a second surface, which is the echo-propagation failure G-012 exists to prevent.

options.option: Edit the original record in place
options.consequence: Produces the tidiest ledger and is the one option forbidden: decisions.jsonl has a sanctioned writer, and hand-editing state to make a record read better is mixed-mode drift.

reasoning: Orchestrator authority: a bookkeeping correction to the orchestrator's own prior record, touching no human-required class. It strengthens verification by removing a non-reproducible number from the set's inheritance rather than reducing anything. Recorded as a decision rather than a silent fix because the alternative -- editing the append-only journal -- is exactly the mixed-mode drift the constitution forbids, and a future reader should be able to see that the stale parenthetical was noticed and handled by the sanctioned route.

question: Spec Session 2 step 3 requires exactly one of: (a) the severity RUBRIC under-discriminates and should be sharpened, (b) the GATE reads the wrong signal and should read something else, or (c) neither - 92% Major is accurate, the findings are genuinely material, and the loop's cost is the honest price of the guarantee. The premise re-derived cleanly this time: 715 of 771 findings are Major (92.7%), stable at 92.7% under two sensitivity variants, with exactly 28 non-canonical values - the figure the spec named. But the measurement went further than the spec anticipated. The field has taken one blocking value for 281 consecutive findings in the ledger era (Major 98.6%, Critical 1.4%, Minor 0); the last Minor any verifier assigned is Set 082 on 2026-07-06, 49 sets and 698 findings ago; is_blocking_issue is TRUE on 100% of findings from round 3 onward; classify_blocking says CONTINUE on 406 of 413 rounds; and across 249 ledgered rounds the field has changed the course of exactly ONE - a round whose deciding Minor was written by the Set 119 doc-only cap rather than by a verifier, and which did not stop the session, since three more rounds ran after it. 106 of the 107 loop terminations in the corpus came from a round that reported no findings at all. Meanwhile the cause is dated and deliberate: ai_router/prompt-templates/verification.md line 93 instructs 'Severity: Critical / Major (a blocking Issue is never Minor - Minor goes under NITS)', shipped by Set 071 S1 on 2026-06-18 and hardened by Set 096 S1 on 2026-07-12, and the Major share by era tracks it exactly (77.6% pre-rubric with 20 Minors, 98.9-100% after, with zero).
decision: (b) - the gate reads the wrong signal. The severity rubric is not under-discriminating by accident and must not be sharpened: sharpening is what produced the present state, so (a) is refuted by the measurement rather than merely rejected. (c) is half right and is reported as such - the findings ARE material, since the loop accepts fixes at 52.3/59.6/59.6% at rounds 3/4/5+ and later rounds are not low-yield - but materiality of the findings does not make the gate informative. The reviewer template already decides continue-or-stop when it decides what is worth reporting as an Issue at all; the Step 7 gate then re-reads that decision from a field the same template forbids from disagreeing with it. 'Only a Critical/Major finding continues the loop' is, in this corpus, operationally identical to 'any reported finding continues the loop', which is what the machinery does anyway. SCOPE OF WHAT THIS SESSION TAKES ON THAT BASIS: nothing that touches the gate. This session ships only the step 4 closed-vocabulary fix at the writer, which strengthens the contract and changes no blocking decision - the machinery's 'unknown' sentinel is removed in favour of key omission (identical reader behaviour, one spelling per meaning), 'Suggestion' is removed from a shipped prompt template that was offering a token no reader knows, and the submit_verdict tool schema's untyped severity string is closed to the canonical three. Every remedy that would change what the gate reads, and therefore could make the loop stop earlier, is referred to the operator as an education-mode brief with the measurement attached, and Session 3 may not take it without an operator ruling.

options.option: (b) the gate reads the wrong signal - named as the defect, with every gate remedy referred to the operator and only the writer-side vocabulary fix taken (chosen)
options.consequence: Reports what the corpus shows without spending the orchestrator's authority on a change it does not hold. The set gains a dated, mechanical explanation for the largest ceremony component's continuation decisions, and Session 3 inherits a named operator decision rather than an unexamined assumption. Costs the session the satisfaction of fixing what it diagnosed. Fully reversible: nothing about the loop's behaviour changes, and a later set or an operator ruling can adopt, amend or reject the diagnosis on the same evidence.

options.option: (a) the rubric under-discriminates and should be sharpened
options.consequence: The option the spec's framing most invites, and the measurement refutes it directly. Pre-consequence-rubric the field carried 77.6% Major and 20 Minors; after Set 095/096 sharpened it, 98.9-100% Major and zero Minors across 49 sets. Sharpening reduced the field's variance every time it was applied, because an anti-nitpick filter is designed to. Choosing (a) would prescribe more of the exact intervention that produced the condition, and would very likely be enacted as another template edit that pushes the field further toward a constant.

options.option: (c) neither - the findings are material and the cost is the honest price
options.consequence: The spec explicitly protects this outcome and half of it survives: the loop's later rounds are not grinding on nothing (56-60% fix-accepted at every depth). But (c) also asserts the machinery is correct, and the gate is not doing the work (c) credits it with. A field that has changed one round's course in 413, via a value its own doc-only cap wrote, is not pricing a guarantee. Choosing (c) would close the question with a true statement about findings standing in for a false one about the gate, and would leave Session 3 believing the continuation decision is examined when it is not.

options.option: (b), and act on it now by changing what the gate reads
options.consequence: Refused, and not on caution: any change to the gate that could make the loop stop earlier is a verification reduction, which is the operator's under the set's hard carve-out and the constitution's four human-required classes, and decision_journal refuses to write it under ai authority. The orchestrator does not get to author its own permission to verify less, however good the measurement behind it is.

reasoning: Judgment-shaped and therefore the orchestrator's under the rubric: it is a spec-vs-reality conflict and the first tiebreak, goal-over-letter, decides it. The spec's LETTER asks which of three named defects applies; its GOAL is that the set act only on measured evidence and that a session concluding the machinery is correct be able to say so without embarrassment. Honouring both means naming (b) while reporting in full the part of (c) that survived - the findings are material - rather than picking the option that flatters the diagnosis. No human-required class is touched by the naming itself: it is a diagnosis, it deletes nothing, and it changes no gate. The verification-reduction carve-out IS touched by the obvious remedy, and that half is deliberately left unexercised and surfaced as an education-mode brief with its measurement, exactly as the spec's non-goals require. Declared verification_effect=strengthens rather than none because what this session actually ships - a closed severity vocabulary enforced at the writer, the removal of a duplicate 'unknown' spelling in favour of key omission, and an enum on a previously unconstrained tool-schema string - tightens the writer contract while leaving every reader lenient about the 28 non-canonical values already committed, and leaves is_blocking_issue's behaviour byte-for-byte unchanged.

question: The Layer 3 run of record (npm run test:playwright) returned 36 passed and 1 failed in a single invocation. The failure is vsix-first-run-walkthrough.spec.ts, which timed out after 300s waiting for the Session Set Explorer's Default module row to read '2 sets' while it still read '0 sets'. Playwright's own output flags the file as slow at 5.2 minutes; run in isolation immediately afterwards the identical spec passes in 46.0 seconds, roughly a seventh of the wall clock it was given under full-suite load. The spec is untouched by this session (last modified in Set 122/123) and drives the extension's TypeScript session-set reader, while this session's entire diff is Python (ai_router/verification.py, verify_session.py, pull_verifier.py), one prompt template and docs. Record Layer 3 as passed on the strength of the isolated re-run, or record the suite as failed?
decision: Record Layer 3 as PASSED, as an explicitly composite run, and state the composition rather than presenting it as a single clean invocation. This is the second worked case in project-guidance G-004, applied verbatim: 'when the declared command executes every test and one fails, re-running that one in isolation and finding it green means every test has executed and passed. Re-running the other thirty adds no coverage, only wall clock.' All 37 Layer 3 tests executed; 36 passed in the full invocation and the 37th passed on isolated re-execution of the identical spec with no code change between the two runs. The recorded run of record carries --detail naming the composition, the failing spec, and the isolated result, so a later reader sees the route rather than a laundered green.

options.option: Record Layer 3 as passed, composite, with the composition stated in the run-of-record detail and the disposition (chosen)
options.consequence: Every Layer 3 assertion has executed and passed, and the evidence stays auditable because the route is written down in three places rather than hidden behind a green token. Costs nothing in coverage. Reversible: the recorded detail names the spec and the two runs, so anyone who doubts the call can re-run the full suite and reach their own conclusion.

options.option: Re-run the entire Playwright suite until one invocation comes back fully green
options.consequence: Produces the tidiest artifact and is what a literal reading of 'one invocation' demands. But it re-executes 36 specs already observed passing to buy nothing, at roughly 8 minutes per attempt on a suite whose own output says the failing file is contention-slow -- so the attempt most likely to succeed is the one that happens to get a quieter machine, which is luck being recorded as evidence. G-004 names this exact trade and rules against it.

options.option: Record the suite as failed and close with a red Layer 3
options.consequence: Maximally conservative and defensible on the bare token. But it would enter a false fact into the record -- that a Layer 3 assertion in this repo does not hold -- when the isolated re-run demonstrates it does. A future session reading a failed run of record would reasonably go hunting for a defect in a Python-only diff that cannot reach a TypeScript tree reader.

options.option: Investigate and fix the flake in this session
options.consequence: Tempting and out of scope. The spec is untouched by this session, the timeout is a load artifact rather than a defect this diff introduced, and the set's own rule bars adding machinery. Correctly a residual with a named owner, recorded in the disposition rather than absorbed here.

reasoning: Judgment-shaped and the orchestrator's under the rubric, decided at tiebreak 1 (goal-over-letter), and it does not touch any human-required class. The GOAL of the run-of-record gate is the question 'did every test execute and pass', not 'did it happen inside one process'. Both halves are satisfied here by direct observation. Critically this is NOT the carve-out: nothing was skipped, no assertion was dropped, no failure went un-re-run, and no bound or gate was relaxed -- which is precisely the line G-004 says this principle must not cross. The one asymmetry worth naming honestly is that the isolated re-run is a different process with different timing, so it is evidence that the assertion holds and not proof that the full-suite path is free of a real race; that residual is recorded rather than argued away, and it is why the composition is stated in the disposition instead of a bare 'passed'.

question: Set 134 S3 cut 1,842 tokens from the 11,644-token preload. Ratchet each per-file ceiling and the total down to the new measurement (leaving zero headroom, as Sets 121 S3/S4 did), or leave slack so the corpus can absorb a future lesson without an operator ceiling raise?
decision: Ratchet every ceiling to measurement: total 11,644 -> 9,802; lessons-learned 2,269 -> 851; project-guidance 3,394 -> 3,245; GEMINI.md 1,922 -> 1,647; session-constitution unchanged at 4,059 (untouched by the cut). The win is banked as 1,842 fewer tokens read EVERY session, not as headroom, and the change-log says so plainly.

options.option: Ratchet every ceiling to measurement (chosen)
options.consequence: Preserves the token-neutral anti-rebloat property the manifest exists to provide: at ceiling, adding prose requires removing prose. Matches the Set 121 S3/S4 precedent exactly and the spec's own instruction that ceilings ratchet down only and lowering after a cut is the point. Cost: the next lesson admitted must be funded by a deletion, same as before. Reversible only by the operator, which is the correct asymmetry.

options.option: Leave the freed 1,842 tokens as headroom under the old ceilings
options.consequence: Would let future sessions absorb new guidance without a deletion. But it converts a measured reduction into permission to re-bloat, and re-bloating to the old ceiling would erase the entire deliverable within a few sets -- which is precisely the operator's standing complaint that every paring attempt ends with the framework larger. Also an orchestrator unilaterally weakening a live gate, which is not its call.

options.option: Ratchet partway, splitting the difference
options.consequence: No principled number exists. Any figure between measurement and the old ceiling is invented, and the manifest's comments would have to record a rationale that is really a preference. Rejected for being unauditable rather than for being wrong.

reasoning: Decided at tiebreak 4 (defer-to-existing-gate). The preload manifest is an existing, CI-enforced gate with a written rule -- ceilings ratchet down only, and 'at ceiling, adding prose requires removing prose' is stated as the mechanism's purpose, not its side effect. The question is therefore already answered by the gate's own contract, and the orchestrator's job is to apply it rather than re-open it. No human-required class is touched: nothing here reduces verification, no external consequence, no value trade-off the framework has not already made explicitly. The mechanism was then exercised on this very session: adding the artifact-cap instruction to session-constitution.md pushed it 2 tokens over its ratcheted ceiling, and 11 characters were removed from the same edit to pay for it.

question: Spec step 3 requires each per-session ceremony artifact to be cut, capped, or justified. Measured corpus-wide: activity-log step descriptions 218,321 words over 3,128 entries (69.8 w/entry); ai-assignment.md 1,582 w/file; sN-conventions.md 1,078 w/file; disposition.json 702 w/file; decisions.jsonl 361 w/decision. Which get capped, and does sN-conventions.md get capped too?
decision: Cap three, exempt two, build nothing. CAP: activity-log step description at 40 words; ai-assignment.md prose at 250 words per session block (route tables exempt); decisions.jsonl at 400 words per decision. EXEMPT: sN-conventions.md and disposition.json. All five rulings are a documented convention in docs/planning/session-set-authoring-guide.md, reachable from the constitution's step-4 pointer row. No validator, no new module.

options.option: Cap the three discretionary-prose artifacts by convention only; exempt the two whose size is set by a reader (chosen)
options.consequence: Returns the measured bloat where it is genuinely discretionary and leaves untouched the two artifacts whose length is dictated by a consumer -- a paid reviewer for the conventions block, close_session's schema for the disposition. Costs nothing in evidence. The risk is that an unenforced convention is ignored, which is real: this set ran at 250.6 w/entry, the WORST of 126 sets, while measuring exactly this.

options.option: Also cap sN-conventions.md, the second-largest artifact at 1,078 w/file
options.consequence: REFUSED, and not on preference. The conventions block is G-010, promoted from L-064-10 precisely because stating the suite baseline and release contract up front stops Round 1 burning findings -- and re-verify rounds -- on an agreed baseline. Shortening the input a paid verifier reads to decide what is a real defect is a verification reduction, which is a hard operator carve-out this set names as an explicit non-goal. Not the orchestrator's to take.

options.option: Enforce the caps with a validator in log_step
options.consequence: Refused. It is the framework's self-diagnosed characteristic failure -- a new governor over the old mechanism -- inside the one session most tempted to build it, and the set's rule is 'no new module'. Set 134 S2 also established the specific hazard: a refusal is only cheap where the caller can retry for free, and log_step is called mid-session inside stateful work.

reasoning: Decided at tiebreak 3 (simpler-code / fewer tests): a documented number beats a module, and the spec independently forbids the module. The interesting half is the refusal. Two of the five artifacts were exempted on evidence rather than trimmed to make the net look better -- sN-conventions.md because capping it would cross into the verification-reduction carve-out that only the operator may authorize, and disposition.json because its shape is owed to a close gate rather than to discretion. A reduction session that cut them anyway would have bought a bigger headline number by quietly spending verification, which is the one currency this set is barred from spending.

This session's diff is Markdown documentation plus preload ceiling numbers in router-config.yaml -- it touches no TypeScript, no fixture, and no extension source. Record Layer 3 as passed, or as failed?

All 37 Layer 3 tests executed; 36 passed in the full invocation and the 37th passed on isolated re-execution of the identical spec with no code change between the two runs.

options.option: Record as passed, composite, with the route written down (chosen)
options.consequence: Every Layer 3 assertion has executed and passed, and the evidence stays auditable because the composition is recorded rather than hidden behind a green token. Costs no coverage. reasoning: Tiebreak 1 (goal-over-letter), and it is the SECOND time this exact call has been made in this set -- Session 2 recorded the identical failure, on the same spec, with the same isolated-re-run result (46.0s then, 45.7s now), against an equally TypeScript-free diff. Two independent sessions reproducing the same load-dependent timeout on the same file is stronger evidence of a contention flake than either alone. This is NOT the verification-reduction carve-out: nothing was skipped, no assertion dropped, no failure left un-re-run, no gate relaxed. question: Session 3 noticed that Set 134 has no ai_router/changelog.d fragment, though Session 2 added public API to ai_router/verification.py (CANONICAL_SEVERITIES, require_severity, canonical_severity_for_write and four siblings) and closed the submit_verdict severity enum. A fragment was drafted. But changelog.d lives under ai_router/, which all three expensive suites declare as `covers`, so adding it staled the pytest, mocha AND playwright runs of record and invalidated the verification evidence stamp -- roughly 20 minutes of suite re-runs plus a routed verification round, to add one Markdown file. Ship the fragment now and pay, or record the gap as a residual?
decision: Record it as a residual with a named owner and do NOT ship the fragment in this session. The gap is real and is written into change-log.md's residual table and the disposition, naming the exact API that lacks an entry, so nothing is concealed. The fragment was removed from the tree, restoring exactly the state that was verified and tested.

options.option: Record the gap as a named residual; do not ship the fragment here (chosen)
options.consequence: Costs nothing and loses nothing that is due today: every entry is [Unreleased] and NOTHING SHIPS in this set, so the changelog is not yet wrong in any consumer-visible way. The recommended next set is a release, which must assemble the changelog anyway -- writing the fragment there costs the same words and zero extra suite time. Risk: a residual can be forgotten, which is precisely the Set 133 S1 failure mode, so it is recorded in two places rather than one.

options.option: Ship the fragment and pay the freshness bill
options.consequence: Re-run pytest (~10 min), mocha (~1 min) and playwright (~9 min), then spend a routed verification round to re-stamp the evidence -- about 20 minutes of wall clock and one paid round, to move a paragraph earlier in time. The suites cannot fail differently: a Markdown file under changelog.d is unreachable from any assertion in any of the three. This is verification theatre, and it is the exact cost class Session 1 measured as C3.

options.option: Ship the fragment and skip re-running the staled suites
options.consequence: REFUSED outright. That is recording a run of record against a tree it did not run on, which is a verification reduction and a hard operator carve-out. Not available to the orchestrator at any price.

reasoning: Tiebreak 1 (goal-over-letter), applying project-guidance G-004 within the line it forbids crossing. The GOAL of a changelog fragment is that a release describes itself truthfully; the goal is met if the fragment exists when something ships, and nothing ships here. The letter -- write the fragment in the session that noticed the gap -- would cost ~20 minutes of suite time and a paid routed round for a file that no assertion in any suite can reach. Critically this is NOT the carve-out: no test was skipped, no assertion dropped, no stale run recorded as fresh. The opposite -- the tree was restored to exactly the state the suites and the cross-provider verifier actually saw, so the evidence is MORE faithful, not less. The residual carries a named owner and appears in both change-log.md and disposition.json, because an unrecorded residual is how Set 133 S1's missing entry happened in the first place. Worth naming for whoever reads this later: the freshness gate treats a Markdown file under ai_router/ as a code change because `covers` is by path. That is a coarse but honest rule and it is not being challenged here; it is simply expensive at the very end of a session, and the cheap answer is to write changelog fragments EARLY, before the suites run, not after.
